_comment: docs/contracts.md:13 requires request hashing over canonicalised JSON (RFC 8785 / JCS), never over raw bytes; docs/contracts.md:17 fixes the exact field set for the execution payload_hash and requires T02 to freeze both the inputs and the resulting bytes.

The expected values live in expected-hashes.json and must be reproduced byte-for-byte by Java (com.resolveflow.shared.contract.CanonicalJson) and Python (resolveflow.contracts.canonical). The two implementations were written independently on purpose: agreement between them is evidence, agreement of one implementation with itself would not be.
Money is integer minor units everywhere. contracts.md:19 forbids float money and caps revisions at 2^53-1; both languages therefore refuse a float rather than rounding it.

refund-with-runtime-fields-present._comment: payload_hash, entitlement_id, trace_id and sent_at are filled in after the hash is computed and must not change it (docs/contracts.md:17).

refund-non-ascii-and-control-chars._comment: Exercises JCS string escaping and UTF-8 output on both sides: escaped control characters, non-BMP code points and a surrogate pair.

utf16-key-ordering._comment: Keys chosen so code-point order and UTF-16 code-unit order differ: U+FFFD (BMP) and U+E000 (BMP) against U+10000 (supplementary). JCS requires UTF-16 order, and a naive code-point sort produces different bytes.

nested-null-and-boolean._comment: null must canonicalise to the literal null rather than being dropped, and booleans must not be serialised as integers.

float-amount._comment: contracts.md:19 forbids float money; both languages must refuse it rather than round it.

missing-hashed-field._comment: A field covered by the hash that is absent must fail loudly; otherwise two different payloads could hash the same.

unknown-action._comment: Only REFUND and RESHIP exist; an unknown action has no field set and no hash.

revision-beyond-the-exact-range._comment: docs/contracts.md:19 caps revisions at 2^53-1 because that is the largest integer Java, Python and JavaScript hold exactly. One beyond it must be refused rather than serialised to a value the other language would round.

control-and-supplementary._comment: Expected canonical text is frozen in expected-hashes.json so both sides are compared on bytes, not on a parsed structure that could hide escaping differences.
